description:
src/lib.rs:149-150 marks the outer `Error` enum as `#[non_exhaustive]`, which
allows adding new variants without a breaking change. But two of the
variants are struct variants with named fields:

    ProfileViolation { reason: Cow<'static, str> },
    OcspDelegation   { reason: Cow<'static, str> },

Neither variant is itself marked `#[non_exhaustive]`. Without that
attribute on the variant, the destructuring pattern
`Error::ProfileViolation { reason }` exhaustively binds the variant's
fields — meaning a caller's pattern match like:

    match err {
        Error::ProfileViolation { reason } => log(reason),
        // ...
    }

will fail to compile if pkix-chain adds a second field (e.g. an
`rfc_section: &'static str` so callers can recognise *which* RFC
invariant was violated, or a `severity` enum to distinguish hard fail
from advisory).

Since the rustdoc on both variants explicitly says \"pattern-match on
the variant rather than the inner string,\" the maintainer is
encouraging the use pattern that is most fragile under field
additions. The two safe options are:

a) Add `#[non_exhaustive]` to each struct variant:

       #[non_exhaustive]
       ProfileViolation { reason: Cow<'static, str> },

   This works since Rust 1.40 and forces callers to write
   `Error::ProfileViolation { reason, .. }`.

b) Wrap the payload in a `#[non_exhaustive]` struct:

       ProfileViolation(ProfileViolationDetail),

       #[non_exhaustive]
       pub struct ProfileViolationDetail {
           pub reason: Cow<'static, str>,
       }

(a) is cheaper and matches the existing `#[non_exhaustive]` on the
outer enum. (b) is conceptually cleaner but adds a public type that
must itself be maintained.

Note: `Error::Path(_)` / `Error::Revocation(_)` / `Error::Identity(_)`
/ `Error::Aia(_)` / `Error::PathBuild(_)` are tuple variants whose
inner type is itself `#[non_exhaustive]`, so they're fine — adding a
new field to those upstream errors doesn't break this enum.

Caller impact: anyone matching specifically on ProfileViolation /
OcspDelegation (the latter is the only programmatic way to recognise
\"RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2 delegation failed\").
title: Error::ProfileViolation and ::OcspDelegation struct variants not non_exhaustive
